summary: A correctness hotfix for the three release blockers: the published orbitdb carve, the stdlib SSE probe, and the transport Vec[Vec]/UDP suites.

highlights.title: Aggregate ownership across literals, returns and helpers
highlights.text: Nested struct literals, implicit tail returns and leaf-helper returns (ok_outcome(done)) now transfer the owned Vec fields; a projected Vec field moves its source aggregate, and a by-value aggregate passed to a retaining callee is moved. The orbitdb carve and the transport Vec[Vec]/UDP suites are green.

highlights.title: Aggregate Vec fields re-read at drop
highlights.text: A struct field's data pointer is loaded at drop time instead of being captured at the binding, so growing the field in place no longer double-frees (p_wave162). The borrowed-but-grown aggregate UAF is covered by the implicit-return transfer above.

highlights.title: Non-owning channel storage
highlights.text: sync.channel now stores its queue as raw element storage (data pointer, len, alloc_cap, cap, closed) instead of a Vec[T]. The handle form copies the cell through ptr.read / ptr.write, and a Vec field made the cell and the local copy two owners of the same items buffer (heap corruption on open/send/free, REL-20261028-1533-stdlib / REL-20261028-1617-stdlib). Elements are moved element-wise on growth and freed by channel_handle_free; the public function API is unchanged.

highlights.title: Server-side SSE
highlights.text: sse_encode_event, sse_encode_comment and sse_encode_heartbeat build LF wire bytes (CR/LF injection rejected; multi-line data becomes repeated data: fields), and sse_write_event, sse_write_comment and sse_heartbeat write them over a TcpStream with write_all. Probe p_wave298_sse_wire covers round-trip, injection and a loopback write.

highlights.title: HTTP/2 connection multiplexing and frame I/O
highlights.text: H2Connection adds a concurrency cap, local stream ids, received-GOAWAY drain (streams above the peer's last id are dropped; an increased last id is rejected) and local graceful drain. xiom/net/h2_io.xi adds a buffered H2Reader over a TcpStream (9-byte header plus payload reassembly, EOF/max_payload errors), h2_join_header_block (HEADERS + CONTINUATION with a block cap), h2_write_frame, h2_write_settings_ack, h2_write_ping_ack and h2_write_header_block (fragmented HEADERS/CONTINUATION). This completes the h2 primitive layer; frame I/O stays with the caller. Probes p_wave298_h2_conn_mux and p_wave299_h2_io.

highlights.title: Request parsing without the whole-head copies
highlights.text: net.server.server_parse_request parses directly from the request byte buffer using (start, len) spans instead of copying the whole head into a Vec[UInt8] and a Str, then slicing request-line strings and two strings per header. Header names are lowercased in the same copy and the header vector is pre-sized. 50k-parse measurement on the official v0.64.8/v0.65.2 compilers (Windows x64): about 8,954 B/iteration before, about 857 B/iteration after; API and error semantics are unchanged. Probe p_http_parse_alloc (REL-20261027-1955-pulse-2).

known_issues: Map/JSON/enum-tree retention (REL-1704) is the next memory slice.
Vec[Str] element strings and removal containers are not yet reclaimed.
By-value aggregate parameters are caller-transferred for retaining callees; callee-side parameter drops remain future work.
